description:
fz-hwn.22 made a boxed first-class callable's VALUE shape carry its single value lane (capture_lanes=[value_lane]). The out-of-band FirstClassPublication seam machinery still bolts the SAME value_lane onto each carrier position (published_value_lane), so the two now duplicate: the maplist+phi plan shows FirstClassPublication seams coexisting with shape-driven lanes (one is picked via position_width's publication preference).

Investigate retiring the redundant path so carrier lanes derive uniformly from the shape:
- position_publication_lanes / function_entry_publication_lanes
- the published_value decode branches (bind_executable_inputs, bind_entry_input)
- position_width's publication preference
- the FirstClassPublication seam emission (jobs/transport.rs ~1031-1104)

Caveat: not every publication use is the boxed-value case (ResumePayload, ReturnPayload, ExternBoundary). Verify each before deleting; this is an investigation + simplification, not a blind removal. Proven by full lib+matrix green with the machinery gone or provably reduced. Depends on fz-hwn.24.

comments.text: Premise DISPROVEN. Collapsing the FirstClassPublication value-lane machinery is not viable: removing the emission breaks 45 tests across spawn/extern/resources/return-payloads and first-class captures. The publication value lane is the load-bearing marshaling interface for fz<->extern boundaries and the path the native decode consumes for carriers; it is NOT redundant with the shape carrying the lane (they are not interchangeable). Salvaged the one genuinely-dead piece: callable_function_entry_publication_lanes (the zero-width-capture arm, never fires post-fz-hwn.22) -- removed in commit 7699794ca.

title: Collapse the redundant FirstClassPublication value-lane machinery now that the shape carries the boxed lane
